text: The patient, a 19-year-old female, presented with stinging pain when peeing for a few days and some cramping pain lower down in her tummy, with a little bit of blood in her urine.
rationale: non-pregnant woman aged 16 or over with lower UTI: back-up or immediate antibiotic

text: Advice was given to drink plenty of fluids and try cranberry juice to flush the infection out.
rationale: self-care advice for everyone with a lower UTI

text: She was advised to review if symptoms persist or if fever, back pain, or vomiting develop.
rationale: reassess if symptoms worsen; refer if signs of a more serious illness

text: The plan is to prescribe a three-day course of trimethoprim or nitrofurantoin.
rationale: antibiotic choice follows the guideline's table for non-pregnant women

text: The plan is to increase furosemide to one tablet twice a day, arrange a blood test for full blood count and kidney function, and organise an echocardiogram.
rationale: diuretics for fluid overload symptoms in heart failure, dose adjusted to need

text: The patient presented with chest discomfort described as pressure and diffuse pain over the pectorals, radiating to the left arm and shoulder, accompanied by nausea, sweating, and shortness of breath, and noted the symptoms were currently present.
rationale: symptoms that indicate a possible ACS; emergency referral when pain is current

text: He has an allergy to aspirin causing mild swelling, and advice was given to communicate the aspirin allergy to the hospital team.
rationale: single loading dose of aspirin unless clearly allergic

text: The patient presented with sudden inability to move his left arm and tingling on the left side of his face, noting onset an hour ago, with difficulty swallowing and complicated speech.
rationale: screen sudden neurological symptoms outside hospital with a recognised tool such as FAST

text: The working diagnosis is mini stroke or TIA, and the plan is to refer the patient to a stroke TIA clinic for carotid ultrasound and brain scans.
rationale: suspected TIA: aspirin 300 mg immediately; specialist assessment within 24 hours

text: He takes Microgynon for contraception and presented with a throbbing headache on the left side accompanied by zigzag lines and blurred vision, nausea and vomiting.
rationale: migraine with aura on a combined hormonal contraceptive: do not routinely offer CHC; acute treatment of migraine

text: A headache diary is recommended to identify triggers, with a review in one to two weeks if symptoms persist or worsen.
rationale: headache diary to aid diagnosis and what to record

text: The working diagnosis is a new onset tension-type headache, and the plan is to try a slightly stronger pain relief similar to ibuprofen taken regularly with food alongside paracetamol.
rationale: tension-type headache: simple analgesia (aspirin, paracetamol or an anti-inflammatory)

text: The patient presented with a fairly severe headache for the past four days accompanied by a feeling of fever and a generalised red and itchy rash that blanches when pressed.
rationale: headache with fever: a feature needing evaluation for further investigation or referral

text: The working diagnosis is anxiety, and the plan involves self-referral for talking therapy, arranging basic blood tests to rule out triggers, and a GP follow-up in a week.
rationale: GAD step 2: low-intensity psychological interventions

text: The patient presented with hearing loss, facial numbness on the left side, and occasional dizziness.
rationale: unilateral hearing loss with altered facial sensation on the same side: immediate referral, seen inside a day

text: The patient presented with a four-day history of sore throat, runny nose, and cough, with an initial fever which has now settled.
rationale: acute sore throat and acute cough: usual course and self-care advice

text: A script for amoxicillin was offered if symptoms do not improve within 24 to 48 hours.
rationale: back-up antibiotic prescription and the advice that goes with it

text: She presented with constant lower abdominal pain worsening over a few days, light pink vaginal bleeding two to three weeks after her last period, and a positive pregnancy test taken a month ago.
rationale: pain or bleeding in early pregnancy: referral to the early pregnancy service

text: He stated he had underactive thyroid previously and stopped taking thyroxine after changing law firms, and had not had a blood test in a long time.
rationale: TSH testing; levothyroxine first-line for primary hypothyroidism

text: The working diagnosis is possible multiple sclerosis, and the plan is an urgent neurology referral for a brain scan.
rationale: confirm a neurological episode before referral; refer suspected MS to a consultant neurologist

text: The patient, a 45-year-old female, presented with breathlessness, pain in the right side of the back, a slight fever, and coughing up blood on two occasions.
rationale: unexplained haemoptysis aged 40 and over: suspected cancer pathway referral

text: He reported shortness of breath, lightheadedness, and calf pain with leg swelling.
rationale: signs of DVT: assessment and two-level Wells score

text: The patient presented with diarrhoea for the last three days, loose and watery six or seven times daily, with vomiting at the start of symptoms and a Chinese restaurant visit four days ago as a potential trigger.
rationale: adult gastroenteritis: no NICE guideline in the corpus (CG84 covers under 5s); should retrieve nothing

text: The working diagnosis is a flare-up of eczema, and the plan is to prescribe a stronger steroid and emollients for seven to 10 days.
rationale: adult eczema: no NICE guideline in the corpus (CG57 covers under 12s); a CG57 hit would be a wrong-population result

text: She had recently returned from Vietnam four weeks ago after trekking and cycling in rural areas, and the working diagnosis is suspected malaria or other exotic infection.
rationale: malaria: no NICE guideline; should retrieve nothing

text: The working diagnosis is labyrinthitis, and the plan is to prescribe an anti-sickness tablet three times a day for ten days.
rationale: labyrinthitis: no NICE guideline; should retrieve nothing

text: He denied chest pain, had a dry cough, felt rundown, and reported no fever.
rationale: negated findings: must not retrieve chest pain guidance

text: His father died of bowel cancer ten years ago, and his mother has Type 2 diabetes.
rationale: family history only: must not retrieve colorectal cancer or diabetes management guidance

text: The working diagnosis is a localised allergic reaction to an insect bite, and the plan is to take an antihistamine such as chlorphenamine or cetirizine.
rationale: localised sting reaction: no NICE guideline; an NG258 anaphylaxis hit would be wrong

text: The plan is to continue ice therapy and consider a stronger anti-inflammatory prescription, with a referral to a physiotherapist for assessment.
rationale: overuse knee injury management: no NICE guideline; should retrieve nothing

text: The working diagnosis is a viral illness with a dry cough for five to six days, and the plan is to rest, drink plenty of fluids and take regular paracetamol, returning for review if symptoms persist for two to three days or breathing worsens.
rationale: acute cough from a viral illness: self-care advice, the usual course and when to seek help

text: He presented with deteriorating hearing and tinnitus in the left ear, on and off for six weeks, and the plan is a face-to-face appointment to examine the ear and exclude a physical blockage.
rationale: first presentation with hearing difficulty: exclude wax and infection, then arrange audiological assessment

text: A link to a tinnitus leaflet was provided for the patient to read.
rationale: tinnitus information given throughout care, in formats such as leaflets

text: He presented with a sudden onset severe headache on the left side of the head with blurred vision and zigzag lines, dizziness and nausea, and vomited twice immediately after the headache started.
rationale: unexplained acute severe headache of sudden onset: high suspicion of subarachnoid haemorrhage; a red-flag feature for investigation or referral

text: He has a history of hypothyroidism and takes thyroxine, presenting with two months of low energy, reduced appetite, low mood and poor sleep, and the plan is to book an examination and blood tests.
rationale: symptoms of hypothyroidism on levothyroxine: measure FT4 with TSH; keep TSH in range and adjust the dose if symptoms persist

text: The working diagnosis is a possible urinary tract infection in a 53-year-old man, and the plan is a three-day course of antibiotics twice a day.
rationale: men with lower UTI: immediate antibiotic; choice and course from table 3 for men

text: He uses his preventer inhaler every morning and evening, and the plan for this asthma exacerbation is to increase the brown inhaler to four puffs twice a day and use salbutamol every two to four hours.
rationale: adult on an inhaled corticosteroid whose asthma control deteriorates: increase the ICS dose for seven days, consider quadrupling

text: He has had asthma since school and currently has no inhalers as they ran out, and the plan is to prescribe a salbutamol inhaler, a preventer inhaler and a spacer.
rationale: a short-acting reliever is not prescribed without an inhaled corticosteroid

text: The plan is to await the ambulance team, who will perform an ECG and determine the appropriate hospital destination.
rationale: suspected ACS: 12-lead ECG promptly without holding up transfer

text: He has type 2 diabetes and high blood pressure, and presented with sudden onset of left arm weakness and tingling on the left side of his face.
rationale: sudden onset neurological symptoms: exclude hypoglycaemia as the cause

text: The working diagnosis is suspected stroke, and the plan is to arrange an ambulance to the local hospital where a stroke doctor will assess him.
rationale: suspected stroke: direct admission to a stroke unit

text: He reported a blinding headache for three days, stronger over the right eye, with sensitivity to light, shooting lights in his vision, and occasional stabbing pain when standing quickly.
rationale: headache with features listed for evaluation: pain changing with posture, eye pain with visual symptoms

text: The working diagnosis is a new onset migraine triggered by stress, and the plan is anti-inflammatories along with paracetamol, good hydration, and monitoring for worsening symptoms.
rationale: acute treatment of migraine: triptan with an NSAID or paracetamol, or monotherapy
